findings.title: Stack-less original error test now passes an error with a stack
findings.why_it_matters: The test named 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' no longer exercises that case, so a regression in the fallback goes green. Its fixture changed from a stack-less object to `new Error('original')`, which always carries a stack, so the constructor takes the copy-the-original-stack branch and the only stack assertion (`to.be.a('string')`) passes trivially. For example, simplifying the guard at GraphQLError.js:195 to `if (originalError)` would leave `e.stack` undefined for stack-less originals (the failure the test was written for) while the whole suite stays green. Restoring a stack-less fixture behind an `any` cast, the same device this diff uses in locatedError-test.js, keeps the file type-checking and restores the guard; the stated intent requires every touched test to keep guarding the behavior its name claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the stack-less fixture with a cast so it still type-checks: `const original: any = { message: 'original' };` (same `any` device as `const e: any = new Error(...)` in src/error/__tests__/locatedError-test.js:30; .flowconfig has no [strict] lint section, so `any` is accepted under `@flow strict`). Alternative if a real Error is preferred: `const original = new Error('original'); delete original.stack;` plus `expect(original.stack).to.equal(undefined)` before constructing. Optionally add `expect(e.stack).to.not.equal(original.stack)` to make the 'new stack' claim explicit.
evidence: src/error/__tests__/GraphQLError-test.js:57 -- it('creates new stack if original error has no stack', () => {
src/error/__tests__/GraphQLError-test.js:61 -- expect(e.stack).to.be.a('string');  (only stack assertion; true for a copied stack as well as a freshly captured one)

src/error/GraphQLError.js:195-202 -- if (originalError && originalError.stack) { Object.defineProperty(this, 'stack', { value: originalError.stack, ... }) } else if (Error.captureStackTrace) { Error.captureStackTrace(this, GraphQLError); }  -- with a real Error the first branch runs; the `&& originalError.stack` fallback the test is named for is never reached
Base version (git show 5384d21:src/error/__tests__/GraphQLError-test.js) -- const original = { message: 'original' };  -- a stack-less value that forced the fallback branch

Scenario: change line 195 to `if (originalError)`. Old test: original.stack is undefined, e.stack becomes undefined, `to.be.a('string')` fails. New test: original.stack is a string, e.stack is that string, assertion passes. The preceding test 'uses the stack of an original error' (lines 41-55) already covers the has-stack path, so the changed test is now a weaker duplicate of it and no test in src passes a stack-less originalError.
provenance: 7e39a12 Ivan Goncharov 2018-11-21 - Enable Flow typings on errors tests + Fix typing for Error constructor (the reviewed commit introduced the fixture change)

residual_risks: Flow was not run (environment forbids it), so whether the five files actually type-check under flow-bin 0.86.0 after the `@noflow` to `@flow strict` switch is unverified from this review; in particular the `// $FlowFixMe` at src/jsutils/__tests__/inspect-test.js:31 suppresses every Flow error on the `String.raw` line and its necessity could not be confirmed (the same suppression precedent exists at src/utilities/__tests__/schemaPrinter-test.js:178, and the .flowconfig suppress_comment pattern does match it).
